sum: Доброе утро, хорошие люди. Страны Персидского залива потратили два десятилетия на экспорт капитала. Теперь он делает обратное: просит больше иностранных денег для финансирования своих проектов внутри страны.

Чиновники, глобальные инвесторы и распределители капитала вчера воспевали регион и его устойчивость даже в условиях кризиса в Bloomberg Invest. Сейчас, похоже, позиция заключается в том, что потребности региона в капитале только растут и что суверенные инвесторы не могут – и не должны – оплачивать счета в одиночку. Да, суверенные и квази-суверенные государства могут вкладывать больше капитала во внутренние активы, чем в международные, но мы также увидим гораздо больше партнерских отношений с иностранными инвесторами.

«Я вижу [возможности] для привлечения стороннего капитала способами, которых мы не делали в прошлом», — заявил на сцене министр инвестиций Мохамед Хасан Алсувайди. Предлагаемые проекты включают энергетические маршруты вокруг Ормузского пролива, новые порты на восточном побережье, центры обработки данных и искусственный интеллект.

Выступавшие утверждали, что война усилила, а не ослабила аргументы в пользу инвестиций в регион. Он показал, насколько региону необходимо диверсифицировать источники поступления денег и маршруты экспорта.

Глобальные финансовые менеджеры рады помочь. Blackstone в этом году разместила в регионе больше капитала, чем когда-либо прежде, сказал глобальный операционный директор Private Wealth Фархад Карим. Что касается инфраструктуры искусственного интеллекта, он говорит, что компания «удваивается, утраивается, учетверяется», несмотря на опасения по поводу устойчивости инфраструктуры после того, как центры обработки данных Amazon Web Services в Дубае и Бахрейне подверглись нападению в начале этого года.

Тем не менее, девелоперы региона все чаще отправляют свои работы за границу. Алаббар говорит, что Индия будет в центре его внимания в течение следующих пяти лет. А Хуссейн Саджвани из Damac сообщил, что подразделение центров обработки данных разработчика ведет переговоры о земельных участках для центров обработки данных в Великобритании и Австралии, помимо трех объектов в США, которые компания уже приобрела.

В сегодняшнем выпуске: Наша Леде спрашивает, готовы ли дороги и правила ОАЭ для беспилотных автомобилей, после того, как на этой неделе было снято, как робот-такси застрял лицом в другую сторону. Плюс: суд ADGM признал основателя NMC Б.Р. Шетти и бывший генеральный директор Прасант Мангхат несут ответственность за восьмилетнее мошенничество, при этом стартовая сумма их долга составляет 5,4 млрд долларов США.

sum: Emaar Properties has not slowed down on its developments despite increase in construction costs, its CEO said, adding that it is delivering ahead of time.

Mohamed Alabbar, the founder of Emaar Properties and e-commerce platform Noon.com, explained that while construction material costs increased by 5 per cent, he is helping contractors wherever necessary.
“I'm glad contractors are moving on time. In fact, we deliver ahead of time now,” he said during the Bloomberg Invest Dubai event on Thursday.
Stay up to date with the latest news. Follow KT on WhatsApp Channels.

The Emirati business mogul said he will tender “a big tower” until the “situation cools down.” While he did not mention the tower’s name, Emaar Properties earlier in the year announced it will launch a tender for the redesigned Dubai Creek Tower Project.

Because the war started around the same time the tender was meant to be issued, plans were delayed. The Emaar founder is withholding tender plans until the geopolitical situation eases, which S&P Global assumes will continue until 2027.

Traffic in Emaar Malls, which includes the Dubai Mall and Dubai Hills Mall, was down by 10 per cent, whereas it was growing 10 per cent in the past five years. “Still, retailers are very comfortable,” Alabbar said.

Emaar Properties Approves Dh12 Billion Offer To Take Emaar Development Private
sum: The company plans to buy the remaining shares for Dh15 each and delist its subsidiary from the Dubai Financial Market, with investors able to accept the offer until Dec. 10.

DUBAI, (UrduPoint / Pakistan Point News - 9th Nov, 2026) UAE real estate company Emaar Properties has approved a cash offer worth around Dh12 billion, or approximately $3.3 billion, to buy minority shares in its subsidiary Emaar Development. The move aims to bring the residential development business under the group’s full control and pave the way for Emaar Development to be delisted from the Dubai Financial Market. The acquisition has not yet been completed.

Gulf News reported on Nov. 3, citing Bloomberg, that Emaar Properties was considering a potential deal worth billions of dollars. The company announced its intention to make a cash offer on Nov. 4, while details of board approval and a possible delisting emerged on Nov. 5. The National and other financial media also reported the development.
Emaar Properties said it will offer to buy, for Dh15 per share in cash, Emaar Development shares not already owned by Emaar Properties or its subsidiary Emirates Property Holdings Limited.
According to the company’s formal offer, Emaar Properties and its subsidiary jointly own 80.1613% of Emaar Development.
The offer price is about 19.4% higher than Emaar Development’s closing share price of Dh12.56 on Nov. 2. At the proposed price, the company’s total valuation would be approximately Dh60 billion.
Emaar Properties’ cash offer opened on Nov. 6, 2026. Under the current schedule, shareholders can accept it until 3 p.m. UAE time on Dec. 10.

Emaar Development PJSC Beat Revenue Forecasts By 17%: Here's What Analysts Are Forecasting Next
sum: As you might know, Emaar Development PJSC (DFM:EMAARDEV) just kicked off its latest third-quarter results with some very strong numbers. It was a decent earnings report, with revenues and statutory earnings per share (EPS) both performing well. Revenues were 17% higher than the analysts had forecast, at د.إ8.8b, while EPS of د.إ0.88 beat analyst models by 12%. Earnings are an important time for investors, as they can track a company's performance, look at what the analysts are forecasting for next year, and see if there's been a change in sentiment towards the company. So we gathered the latest post-earnings forecasts to see what estimates suggest is in store for next year.

After the latest results, the ten analysts covering Emaar Development PJSC are now predicting revenues of د.إ36.6b in 2027. If met, this would reflect a notable 14% improvement in revenue compared to the last 12 months. Statutory earnings per share are predicted to rise 7.7% to د.إ3.60. Yet prior to the latest earnings, the analysts had been anticipated revenues of د.إ36.6b and earnings per share (EPS) of د.إ3.87 in 2027. The analysts seem to have become a little more negative on the business after the latest results, given the small dip in their earnings per share numbers for next year.

It might be a surprise to learn that the consensus price target was broadly unchanged at د.إ16.99, with the analysts clearly implying that the forecast decline in earnings is not expected to have much of an impact on valuation. That's not the only conclusion we can draw from this data however, as some investors also like to consider the spread in estimates when evaluating analyst price targets. The most optimistic Emaar Development PJSC analyst has a price target of د.إ22.00 per share, while the most pessimistic values it at د.إ13.50. There are definitely some different views on the stock, but the range of estimates is not wide enough as to imply that the situation is unforecastable, in our view.

Of course, another way to look at these forecasts is to place them into context against the industry itself. It's pretty clear that there is an expectation that Emaar Development PJSC's revenue growth will slow down substantially, with revenues to the end of 2027 expected to display 11% growth on an annualised basis.

Emaar Properties plans to buy out Emaar Development for $3.3 billion — The National
sum: In Dubai, Emaar Properties has approved a plan to buy back the shares of developer Emaar Development that it and its subsidiary EPHL do not yet own, for about 12 billion dirhams ($3.3 billion). After the deal is completed, Emaar Properties plans to delist Emaar Development from the Dubai Financial Market, The National reports.

Emaar Properties offered 15 dirhams for each Emaar Development share not owned by Emaar Properties and EPHL. This represents a 19.4% premium to the closing price of 12.56 dirhams on November 2, the last trading day before the announcement of the board meeting.

Emaar Development has 4 billion ordinary shares. Emaar Properties and its subsidiary EPHL own more than 3.2 billion of them, or nearly 81%. The remaining more than 793.5 million shares are valued at more than 11.9 billion dirhams under the offer. On Thursday, Emaar Development shares fell by about 0.4% to 14.52 dirhams.

In a stock exchange filing, Emaar Properties said the offer was driven by “strategic considerations”. The company said that acquiring the remaining shares would enable it to fully integrate the UAE development business into the group structure and manage and finance it within a unified capital allocation system.

Emaar Development also reported third-quarter profit of 3.5 billion dirhams, nearly 8% higher than a year earlier. Its revenue rose 14% to 8.8 billion dirhams. UAE property sales for the first nine months amounted to 26.2 billion dirhams, while international sales of development projects totalled 8.5 billion dirhams.

Separately, Emaar Properties reported a 5.6% increase in net profit attributable to the company’s owners in the third quarter, to 4.6 billion dirhams. The company’s revenue for the three months to the end of September rose nearly 3% to 13.6 billion dirhams.

sum: Emaar Properties to delist Emaar Development after Dh12 billion buyout approval

Emaar Properties, based in Dubai, intends to remove its construction division from the emirates stock exchange following board approval of a Dh12 billion ($3.3 billion) buyout designed to streamline the group's operations. In a Thursday filing with the Dubai Financial Market, the developer said it will pay Dh15 per share for the stake it does not already hold in Emaar Development.

Emaar Development's ordinary shares total four billion. Emaar Properties and its subsidiary EPHL own over 3.2 billion of these, representing almost 81 per cent. The roughly 793.5 million shares outside their ownership push the total buyout value above Dh11.9 billion.

The price is 19.4 per cent above Emaar Development's Dh12.56 close on November 2, the final trading session before the board meeting was announced. On Thursday, Emaar Development shares ended about 0.4 per cent weaker at Dh14.52.

Emaar Properties, known for constructing the Burj Khalifa, the world's tallest building, described the offer in the filing as motivated by strategic considerations. According to the company, the transaction would place the UAE development business entirely inside the group, enabling management and funding through one capital allocation framework consistent with its disciplined approach to capital allocation and long-term value creation.

The company also stated that purchasing the Emaar Development shares held outside Emaar Properties and EPHL would let it streamline and unify the group's structure while running the domestic development business in a fully integrated manner across the broader group.
Separately on Thursday, Emaar Development posted third-quarter profit of Dh3.5 billion, a yearly gain of almost 8 per cent. Revenue for the quarter climbed 14 per cent to Dh8.8 billion.

sum: The 194-residence development in Gomti Nagar Extension marks the company's second premium high-rise project in Lucknow, following Elite Oasis

Emaar India on Monday launched a new luxury residential project in Lucknow, with prices starting at Rs 2.15 crore, as the Dubai-based real estate group's Indian arm looks to strengthen its presence in the city's premium housing market.

Named Elara, the project is located at Emaar Gomti Greens in Sector 7, Gomti Nagar Extension, near Shaheed Path. The development will comprise a single 35-storey tower offering 194 premium three-bedroom residences.
Elara marks Emaar India's second project in the premium high-rise residential segment in Lucknow, following the launch of Elite Oasis in June 2025 in the same township.
The company said Elite Oasis had received a strong response from homebuyers, prompting it to introduce another premium residential development in the market.
Designed by Ideate Design Studio, Elara is an IGBC pre-certified Gold project. Construction is scheduled for completion by September 2031, according to the company.
The project will offer three configurations of three-bedroom apartments, with select residences positioned to offer views of the Gomti River.

In a first, Indians can book Burj Khalifa, Singapore's Universal Studios tickets via UPI | Here's how to book
sum: Indian tourists visiting Dubai and Singapore can now make online ticket payments using India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI). The Finance Ministry recently announced that the facility is available for Burj Khalifa and Singapore attractions, including Universal Studios Singapore, Singapore Oceanarium, and Adventure Cove Waterpark.

Citing a Finance Ministry statement, PTI reported that the initiative aims to simplify international travel bookings for Indians by allowing them to use their preferred UPI applications for online payments at these destinations.

UPI payments for online bookings were enabled through partnerships announced by NPCI International Payments Ltd (NIPL) in the UAE on 29 July and in Singapore on 9 September. NIPL is the international arm of the National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI).

In the UAE, UPI acceptance has been enabled for ‘At the Top’, Burj Khalifa, in collaboration with NEOPAY and Emaar Entertainment. The statement said it is the first attraction in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to implement UPI for e-commerce.

In Singapore, UPI payments have been enabled at Resorts World Sentosa through a partnership with payment institution FOMO Pay. The facility covers bookings for major attractions at Resorts World Sentosa, including Universal Studios Singapore, the Singapore Oceanarium and Adventure Cove Waterpark.

Stock markets in the United Arab Emirates extended their losses on Friday as fears of a wider regional conflict weighed on investor sentiment. Dubai's benchmark index fell 1.4% to a more than four-month low, while Abu Dhabi's index declined 1.2%. Real estate stocks, including Emaar Properties and Aldar Properties, recorded losses alongside banking and energy-related shares. The declines followed Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia that heightened concerns about regional security and energy supply disruptions. Both Dubai and Abu Dhabi indexes also ended the week lower.

Stock markets in the United Arab Emirates fell on Friday, with Dubai recording the sharper decline as losses in banking and real estate shares weighed on the market. Investor sentiment weakened amid fears of a wider regional conflict following Houthi strikes in Saudi Arabia.

Saudi Aramco has reportedly asked employees to evacuate its headquarters in Dhahran and work remotely, according to six people familiar with the matter. The move came a day after an attack on a nearby airport killed two people, adding to concerns about security risks in the region.

Dubai's main index dropped 1.4% to its lowest level in more than four months. Emirates NBD Bank, the emirate's largest lender, fell 3.5%, while blue-chip property developer Emaar Properties declined 2.1%.

Dar wa Emaar signs sponsorship partnership with Al Qadsiah Club
sum: Dar wa Emaar Real Estate Development and Investment Company announced the signing of a sponsorship partnership with Al Qadsiah Club. Under the partnership, the company becomes the club’s Official Real Estate Development Partner, with its logo appearing on the sleeves of the club’s kits across the first football team, the women’s team, and Al Qadsiah Academy.

This partnership stems from a shared geographical connection and common vision between Dar wa Emaar and Al Qadsiah Club, as both originate from the Eastern Province and share an ambition to contribute to building a more impactful and sustainable future. While Al Qadsiah continues to strengthen its position as one of the Kingdom’s ambitious sporting institutions through a modern identity and growing fan base, Dar wa Emaar continues to play its role in developing integrated residential communities that enhance quality of life and respond to the aspirations of Saudi families.

The partnership reflects the alignment of sports and urban development visions through a national model that brings together two Eastern Province institutions – one contributing to building communities, and the other to nurturing talent and strengthening sporting presence – in a way that aligns with Saudi Vision 2030’s objectives of enhancing quality of life, empowering the sports sector, and supporting sustainable development.

On this occasion, Osama Al Khunaizi, CEO of Dar wa Emaar, said: “Our sponsorship of Al Qadsiah Club stems from our deep belief in the importance of supporting national institutions that share our roots and sense of belonging. Both Dar wa Emaar and Al Qadsiah originate from the Eastern Province, carrying its spirit, ambition, and active contribution to the Kingdom’s development journey.

We view this partnership as a natural extension of our role as a national company committed to developing integrated communities. We also believe that sports represent a key pillar in enhancing quality of life and strengthening a sense of belonging.

items.t: Gulf stock markets surge after US and Iran agree to ceasefire
sum: Stock markets across the Gulf rose sharply on Wednesday, as a dramatic de-escalation in the US-Israeli war on Iran and the growing prospect of a permanent peace deal buoyed investor sentiment.

The rally follows the US and Israel agreeing to halt strikes for two weeks, with Tehran in turn saying it would allow vessels to pass through the Strait of Hormuz “via co-ordination with Iran's armed forces”. The move has eased fears that the global energy crisis would worsen.

In the UAE, Dubai’s equities benchmark, the DFM General Index, surged more than 8 per cent during early trade, ending the session 6.9 per cent higher. It was supported by a nearly 13 per cent rise in the shares of Emaar Properties, the emirate's biggest developer.
Dubai’s leading lender Emirates NBD also ended the session 10.6 per cent higher, while Dubai Islamic bank, the biggest Sharia-compliant bank in the Emirates, added 6 per cent.

On the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange, the main stocks index advanced as much as 4.6 per cent in early trade, before closing up 2.8 per cent. A 10 per cent surge in Aldar Properties helped the market. Banking stocks in the UAE capital also rallied, with First Abu Dhabi Bank adding 5 per cent, while Abu Dhabi Commercial Bank and Abu Dhabi Islamic bank advanced 5.1 per cent and 10.48 per cent, respectively.

The equities rallied after US President Donald Trump said in a post on Truth Social that he agreed to “suspend the bombing and attack of Iran for a period of two weeks”, after talks with Pakistan. He said the deal was subject to Tehran immediately allowing safe passage through the strait.
“We received a 10-point proposal from Iran and believe it is a workable basis on which to negotiate,” Mr Trump added.

Dubai realty: Why the ‘crash’ narrative does not add up
sum: “Right time for Indians to ‘fly, buy, Dubai?” a senior Indian journalist wrote.

“Dubai real estate lost nearly a fifth of its value over the last 10 days erasing all year-to-date gains and is threatening to reverse its 2025 gains which provide a mere 15% additional downside cushion before prices would revert to 2024 levels,” he added.
“Dubai and UAE are cooked. Dubai Real Estate down 60%,” wrote a trader and investor.
Both share a screenshot of a sharp fall in the DFM Real Estate Index. And truth be told, if you judge by the screenshot, the situation does look alarming.

“It is a buyer’s market, and that’s completely flipped,” Andrew Cummings, Head of Residential Agency - ME for Savills ME, admits. Dubai Real Estate, which has delivered hockey-stick growth since COVID, has definitely slowed. Sellers aren’t selling and are holding on. Transaction volumes are down roughly 25–30% between February and March, and new leads and searches have dropped well over 50%. Interest from Indian buyers, however, continues to remain strong — particularly among those actively looking for deals in moments like this.

If you search on FB Marketplace or even Instagram, you come across listings with the dreaded D word ‘distress’. But they are all buildings that are under construction, and barring 1 or 2, are offering deals less than 10% of the Original Price offered.

But here is where it gets very interesting. A quick search of 4 prominent areas of Dubai (Dubai Hills, Business Bay, Citywalk & Palm Jumeirah) showed an increase of 4–13% on prices between March and previous months, a moderate decline of 1–5% on some properties, and one out of the 20 showed a decline of 17% compared to a similar property sold in the market pre-conflict. All this data is public, and we used DXB interact for it.

items.t: Neha Saxena Shenoy joins Emaar India to lead people strategy
sum: Emaar India names Neha Saxena Shenoy as CHRO as the developer sharpens its talent strategy and organisational capability for expansion.

Emaar India has appointed Neha Saxena Shenoy as Chief Human Resources Officer, in a move aimed at strengthening its people strategy as the real estate developer scales operations across key Indian markets.

The company said Shenoy will lead the HR agenda with a focus on talent strategy, leadership development, organisational transformation and building a high-performance culture aligned with business growth.
Shenoy joins Emaar India from Info Edge India, where she served as Executive Vice President and worked on people strategy and organisational effectiveness across business units.
Before that, she was Deputy CHRO at Cairn Oil and Gas, where she led talent strategy, employee experience, HR shared services, and diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives for a large workforce.

Her appointment comes as companies in capital-intensive sectors, including real estate and infrastructure, place greater emphasis on leadership pipelines and workforce capability to support expansion plans.
Shenoy has held senior HR leadership roles across multiple industries. She served as Human Resources Director at Honeywell, leading HR strategy for several large business units.

sum: Egypt’s 50 Most Valuable Companies 2026Waqar Mughal2026-03-26T09:14:09+00:00
Egypt’s stock market staged a sharp rebound in 2025, with total market capitalisation rising more than 40% to $67.3 billion as of January 2026.

The country’s 50 most valuable listed companies drove most of that momentum. Together, they accounted for $55.8 billion in market value – around 83% of the entire market. Over the past 12 months, the combined market capitalisation of the top 50 climbed by more than 48%, signalling renewed investor appetite for Egyptian equities.

Industrials led the rally, driven largely by cement and fertiliser producers. Ferchem Misr for Fertilizers & Chemicals posted the strongest gains, with its market value surging after a 746% rise in its share price and a 2,180% increase in paid capital, following its merger with two companies and its move from the SME board to the EGX main market. Misr Cement Group, Sinai Cement, and Misr Beni Suef Cement Company followed, with market value increases of 554%, 264%, and 222%, respectively.

Nearly half of the companies on the list saw their market value rise by more than 50% over the year. Only 10 recorded declines, led by Egyptian Iron & Steel Company, which fell 35% as it remains under liquidation.

Commercial International Bank (CIB) retained its position as Egypt’s most valuable listed company, with a market capitalisation of $9.6 billion, followed by Talaat Moustafa Group Holding and Elsewedy Electric. Banking and financial services was the most represented sector, with 14 companies and a combined market value of $21.2 billion, ahead of industrials, which placed 11 companies with a combined $12.4 billion in market capitalisation.

items.t: Punjab & Haryana HC clears way for FIR against Emaar India in property dispute
sum: Punjab and Haryana HC has refused to quash an FIR against Emaar India Ltd, rejecting the real estate giant's plea. The company faces allegations of cheating, fraud, and criminal conspiracy for allegedly suppressing prior binding agreements over project land. The court found the allegations disclosed a prima facie case requiring investigation.
CHANDIGARH: In a blow to real estate giant Emaar India Ltd, Punjab and Haryana HC has refused to quash an FIR involving allegations of cheating, fraud and criminal conspiracy against the company.

Justice Mandeep Pannu passed the orders while dismissing a petition filed by Emaar India, seeking quashing of a Gurgaon additional chief judicial magistrate order to register an FIR against the company and its officials.

The case stems from a complaint filed by Synergy Finhub LLP, which accused Emaar India and some of its officials of a "well-orchestrated" deception. At the heart of the dispute is the claim that Emaar India deliberately suppressed the existence of prior binding agreements with third parties over the same project land.

Emaar India subsidiaries had allegedly entered into collaboration deals with Tejas Home Build Pvt Ltd in 2013 and Nanny Infrastructure Pvt Ltd as early as 2010. These pre-existing arrangements were allegedly not disclosed to Synergy Finhub at the time of signing their JDA. The complainant alleged they were forced into a Rs 1 crore settlement with Tejas Home Build to resolve third-party claims.

On March 10, the Gurgaon court ordered an FIR, despite a police action taken report suggesting the matter was purely civil. Emaar India challenged the order, arguing the magistrate had ignored police's conclusion that no cognisable offence was made out. The defence contended the dispute was a contractual disagreement already subject to arbitration.

items.t: Emaar Properties shares jump more than 5% as Dubai market extends rebound
sum: Emaar leads gains on Dubai bourse as investors return to heavyweight property stocks amid broader rebound in Gulf equities
Shares of UAE developer Emaar Properties surged more than 5% on Wednesday, helping lift Dubai’s main stock index as investors extended a rebound in Gulf equities despite ongoing regional tensions.
Emaar was among the strongest performers on the Dubai Financial Market, gaining about 5.2% during the session, while market data showed the share price at around 12.10 dirhams ($3.3).
The rally came as Dubai’s benchmark index rose 2.3%, also supported by sharp gains in Emirates NBD.
Emaar's stock price also surged by over 15.7% from Tuesday's low of 10.45 dirhams ($2.85).

The advance marked a further recovery for Emaar after several sessions of steep losses earlier this week, when the company’s shares had come under pressure along with broader UAE equities amid escalating conflict in the region. On Monday, Emaar led losses on the Dubai exchange as investor sentiment weakened sharply.
The latest gains suggest investors are selectively returning to heavyweight UAE property and banking stocks, supported by confidence in the country’s financial stability and domestic fundamentals.

items.t: Dubai stocks enter bear market as conflict-driven selloff hits banks, property shares
sum: Deepening losses in banking, real estate shares amid conflict-driven selloff pushed Dubai’s main index more than 20% below its February peak, sending it into bear-market territory

Dubai’s main stock index slipped into bear-market territory on Monday after falling more than 20% from its February peak as escalating regional tensions triggered broad selling across banking, real estate and travel-linked shares.
The Dubai Financial Market General Index reached a recent high of 6,785.48 on Feb. 10 and later dropped to 5,391.98 on March 13, according to Dubai Financial Market data.
That represents a decline of about 20.5%, meeting the widely used definition of a bear market.

Selling pressure persisted Monday, with Reuters reporting that Dubai’s benchmark fell another 2%, led by a 3% drop in Emaar Properties and a 1.4% decline in Emirates NBD as investors reacted to rising geopolitical uncertainty in the Gulf.
The index has fallen more than 18% since the conflict began.

The downturn has been concentrated in sectors most exposed to domestic economic activity and investor sentiment, particularly banking and real estate, while aviation and tourism-linked stocks have also come under pressure as security concerns cloud the outlook for travel, trade and business activity.

Dubai's property sector falls on the stock exchange
sum: Crisis knocks out Emaar Properties and Aldar Properties (-18%)

It had been a record year, 2025, for real estate in the Emirates. Then, images of the Burj Al Arab hotel in flames, hit by debris from a drone (along with the fire at the Fairmont The Palm hotel on Palm Jumeirah), in Dubai, cracked the skyline and sank the stock markets.

Since the beginning of the conflict, the Dubai Financial Market's (DFM) property index has lost over 17%, marking the steepest decline among sector indicators. After recording returns of 180% since October 2023, it has now wiped out all gains from 2026.

Since the beginning of the conflict, Emaar Properties, one of the largest real estate developers in the Eau as well as builder of the Burj Khalifa, and Aldar Properties, the largest listed developer in Abu Dhabi, have left 18% of their value on the ground.
Both closed yesterday, 10 March, with losses of -4.1 per cent and -3.6 per cent, respectively.

items.t: Iran attacks shake Dubai's high-profile real estate as losses near 20%
sum: UAE's booming property sector in Dubai hit a sudden market shock as a sharp sell-off in property stocks wiped out the sector’s gains for the year amid Iran's barrage that rattled one of the world's leading real estate investment hubs.

The Dubai Financial Market (DFM) Real Estate Index dropped more than 17% since the start of the conflict, marking the steepest decline among sector gauges on the exchange. The broader DFM index also slid, falling about 11% during the same period.

Shares of some of the emirate’s largest property developers led the downturn. Emaar Properties, one of the United Arab Emirates’ biggest real estate developers and the builder of landmarks such as the Burj Khalifa, fell by 13.6%.

Deyaar Development, a Dubai-based developer focused on residential and commercial projects, declined by 11.6%, while Union Properties, another Dubai-listed real estate company involved in large-scale mixed-use developments, dropped by 12.8%. Tecom Group, which operates business districts and commercial property hubs across Dubai, recorded a smaller loss of 2.8%.

Dubai’s property market set a new record in 2025, with real estate transactions in the emirate reaching nearly AED 917 billion ($249.7 billion). The surge reflected strong demand from international buyers, high-net-worth individuals, and expatriates, as the city continued attracting capital with residency incentives, tax advantages, and a steady pipeline of large-scale developments.
Property prices had already been on a prolonged upswing before the latest market turmoil. Since 2021, housing prices in Dubai have steadily increased, delivering a 9.6% real return in 2025.

The recent market downturn comes as fears grow over continued Iranian attacks targeting the United Arab Emirates after the war began on Feb. 28, denting the region’s appeal as a stable destination for international investors and property buyers. Following joint U.S.-Israel strikes on Iran, Tehran launched retaliatory attacks on countries hosting U.S. military bases, expanding the conflict across the Gulf region.

items.t: Emaar founder boldly reveals why Dubai’s property market has ‘nothing to fear’ amid Iran and US-Israel wa
sum: and concerns about economic stability amid US-Israel war against Iran, Dubai’s real estate sector remains resilient, according to leading industry voices. Mohamed Alabbar, the founder of Emaar Properties, recently stated that the Dubai property market has “nothing to fear” even as the region navigates a complex geopolitical environment and prepares for a surge in new housing supply.

The comments come at a time when regional tensions linked to the Iran–US–Israel conflict have raised questions about investor confidence across Gulf markets. Financial markets in the UAE have already experienced volatility following regional security concerns, while analysts have warned that geopolitical risks could test Dubai’s reputation as a safe investment hub.

Yet Alabbar remains optimistic about the long-term outlook for the emirate’s real estate sector. He argued that the UAE’s stable leadership, long-term planning, and strong economic fundamentals have historically helped the country weather global and regional shocks. These factors, he says, continue to make Dubai a safe haven for international capital and property investors.
Dubai property supply surge seen as healthy for the market amid Iran and US-Israel war
Dubai is also preparing for a major wave of new property supply in 2026 and 2027, a development that some analysts fear could soften prices.

However, Alabbar believes additional inventory will actually benefit the market by stabilizing price growth and ensuring sustainable expansion. Rather than a threat, he sees the upcoming supply as a natural part of the property cycle. According to the developer, the market’s long-term strength depends on maintaining balanced growth rather than short-term price spikes.

Recent financial results from Emaar reinforce the positive outlook. The developer reported record property sales and strong revenue growth, driven by sustained demand for residential projects and luxury developments across Dubai. The city’s luxury property segment has also continued to attract wealthy international buyers. Even during regional tensions, high-end real estate transactions have reached record levels, including ultra-luxury apartment sales exceeding hundreds of millions of dirhams.

items.t: UAE’s property sector faces reckoning after Iran strikes
sum: DUBAI - The UAE’s years-long property boom faces its first real test after Iranian missile strikes shattered the Gulf’s safe-haven aura, rattling investors and exposing how heavily Dubai and Abu Dhabi rely on offshore money to sustain their building spree.

The attacks on airports, ports and residential areas in both cities have punctured the region’s reputation for stability at a moment when concerns about overheating were already surfacing. Developers that had been selling out off-plan launches within hours now confront a sharply changed demand backdrop.

Off-plan deals made up 65 per cent of Dubai transactions in 2025, according to Betterhomes, meaning most purchases were for homes not yet built. That pipeline may now face a far tougher market, with foreign appetite set to be the decisive factor.

On March 4, shares in Dubai and Abu Dhabi developers plunged. Aldar Properties, Abu Dhabi’s largest listed developer, and Emaar Properties, the force behind downtown Dubai and the Burj Khalifa, both fell 5 per cent, while bond prices of major developers dropped sharply.
Bond markets – a critical funding channel for UAE developers – are now effectively shut for new issuance, with spreads widening across the sector.

“In this region, we know things start quickly and end quickly and we overcome this because the fundamentals across the GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) nations are strong,” said Mr Ziad El Chaar, the CEO of Dar Global, the luxury developer behind a string of Trump-branded projects across the Gulf.
Others said the fallout was already visible. A senior real-estate banker told Reuters his firm had this week shelved a planned UAE property capital raising.

items.t: UAE stock markets drop after two-day halt as regional tensions escalate
sum: DFM falls nearly 5% while ADX slips nearly 2% as investors absorb geopolitical risks

The Dubai Financial Market General Index closed down 4.7% on Wednesday, marking its steepest single-day drop since mid 2022. Abu Dhabi equities also moved lower, with the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange ending the day down 2%, after falling as much as 3.6%.

The decline came after regulators halted trading earlier this week while monitoring the escalating conflict involving the United States, Israel and Iran. Markets resumed trading on Wednesday with investors processing several days of global developments at once.
Hamza Dweik, Head of Trading for the MENA region at Saxo Bank, said the initial session reflected a rapid adjustment rather than panic selling.
"When UAE markets reopened after the two day suspension, trading was dominated by price discovery as investors absorbed accumulated global and regional developments."

From a technical perspective, both indices, DFMGI and the FTSE ADX General Index, held above the 200-day EMA levels at Dh6,010 and Dh10,060, with the ADX closing above the 100-day EMA at Dh10,220. If they dip further towards the 200-day EMA tomorrow, a rebound from that level is possible. Tomorrow, DFMGI would need a close above its 100-day EMA level, and ADX will need to hold that level to see a reversal of the recent selloff.
Losses spread across much of the market during the reopening session, particularly among banking, real estate and aviation-related stocks.

UAE bourses slide after markets reopen from two-day halt during Iranian attacks
UAE stocks retreat as regional war continues to rage

Why has the UAE closed its stock exchanges?
sum: The United Arab Emirates has closed its main stock exchanges amid a widening conflict in the region following the United States and Israel’s attacks on Iran.

The UAE’s financial regulator on Sunday announced that its key exchanges in Dubai and Abu Dhabi would not immediately reopen after the weekend break amid the fallout of the US-Israeli attacks that killed Iran’s Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

The announcement that the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange and Dubai Financial Market would remain closed on Monday and Tuesday came after the UAE was hit with hundreds of Iranian missile and drone attacks, including a strike on Abu Dhabi’s main airport that killed one person and wounded seven others.

The UAE’s Capital Markets Authority said in a statement that it would continue to monitor developments in the region and “assess the situation on an ongoing basis, taking any further measures as necessary”.

The financial regulator did not elaborate on the rationale for its decision, only saying that it was taken in accordance with its “supervisory and regulatory role” in managing the country’s financial markets.
While closing the stock market outside of scheduled breaks is relatively unusual worldwide, especially in the era of electronic trading, it is not unprecedented.
Typically, when financial authorities halt stock trading during a crisis, it is because they are concerned about panic selling.

items.t: UAE stock markets to close for two days amid Iran strikes
sum: The United Arab Emirates said its two key markets will close for two days of the week, avoiding a possible meltdown after the Gulf country was repeatedly hit as Iran retaliated against US-Israeli airstrikes.

Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange and Dubai Financial Market will be closed on March 2 and March 3, the UAE Capital Market Authority said in an emailed statement. “The Authority will continue to monitor developments in the region and assess the situation on an ongoing basis, taking any further measures as necessary,” it added.

Dubai and Abu Dhabi have faced hundreds of missiles and drone attacks from Iran, which has been responding to an onslaught from the US and Israel, since Saturday morning. Most have been intercepted and there are few reports of casualties and damage to multiple areas across both cities. But the attacks are causing panic among residents and pose a huge threat to the UAE’s economy and status as a stable financial, logistics and tourism hub.

“US-Israel attacks on Iran threaten demand shocks for UAE property sales, risking absorption of 350,000 units in new supply, as well as 120 million footfalls into Dubai Mall and tourism into retail and hospitality,” Bloomberg Intelligence analysts Edmond Christou and Salome Skhirtladze wrote in a note. “UAE developers, such as Emaar, are vulnerable as are UAE banks with greater cyclical exposure.”
The UAE stock exchanges’ market capitalization stands at $1.1 trillion, making it the 19th largest in the world. It holds a 1.4% weight on MSCI Inc.’s emerging markets benchmark.
Read More: Dubai’s Worst Nightmare Unfolds as Iran Strikes Neighbors

The market closures are unusual in the country. Outside regularly-scheduled holidays, UAE bourses are typically shuttered only during periods of national mourning, such as one that followed the death of President Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan in May 2022.
